answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the ripple schedule in the yarrow ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the cedar checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 128 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 6 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 26 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
